ideas.title: Sled the cart down the dune: plough to brake, lean to steer, tip if you lean wrong
ideas.nearest: A snowball that grows as it rolls, a take that misses
ideas.critique: This round answers the one-dune-rig worry where it matters. The soil's cohesion and friction come from each cell's own moisture and compaction, a check script reproduces published Reece and Wong numbers before anything uses them, and rollover comes from the rigid body's own reactions instead of a fitted threshold. The ruts that persist and the dune behaving differently after rain give the player a reason to come back. The scope is still the risk: a friends' 'pose solved from acceleration' that turns out to be a canned lurch-and-grab, or soil cells that all end up with the same dry-sand values, would turn a shareable ride into a tuned stunt.

ideas.title: Work any metal cold, and what you made decides how the part works
ideas.nearest: A copper wire keeps its bends
ideas.critique: Carrying the thickness and hardness fields into the cell's corrosion and the brush's spring force is what was missing: the uneven sheet now matters later, and per-metal yield, hardening and recrystallisation make it more than a lead rig. The payoff is still delayed, though. This session's film is a close fixed shot of a sheet flattening on a rock, which the island's copper-wire and glass posts have shown before, and the reason to hammer well only becomes visible once the cell and motor exist.
